### meter

Meter — a segmented level with its label and reading on one row. The fraction is the only number: <div class="nk-seg" data-frac="0.22"> draws the segments, and an empty .nk-meter-value is printed from it ("22%", toned like the segments). An amount instead: data-value="22.1" data-max="24" data-unit="G" fills 92% and prints "22.1/24G". Write your own words there to replace the printed reading. <div class="nk-meter"><span class="nk-meter-label">CPU</span><div class="nk-seg" data-frac="0.22"></div><span class="nk-meter-value"></span></div>

- classes: `nk-meter`, `nk-meter-label`, `nk-meter-note`, `nk-meter-value`
- modifiers: `is-mono`
- attributes: `data-tone`

Knob — a rotary control, machined. A recessed bezel (the dial's well) carries one lamp per detent; the raised cap is a shell that turns to the chosen detent, its glyph in that choice's colour. ### primitives

### wheel

Thumbwheel — a ridged drum set edge-on into the panel, like the wheel on a camera. You roll it: drag along it (Shift for fine), scroll over it, or use the arrows; Home and End jump to the ends, double-click returns to data-default. The ridges travel with the value and the drum is shaded round, so it reads as turning, not sliding. It never shows its position as a bar — the reading beside it does. From Gouache's light controls. <div class="nk-wheel-unit"> <span class="nk-wheel" data-min="0" data-max="359" data-value="120" data-unit="°" aria-label="Light rotation"></span> <output></output> </div> .is-vertical stands it up (roll up and down).

- classes: `nk-wheel`, `nk-wheel-unit`
- modifiers: `is-turning`, `is-vertical`
- attributes: `data-at`

### angle

Angle dial — sets a direction, 0–359°. A recessed well with a notch every 45° (a longer one at 0°), and a raised pointer cap that you grab and turn to face where you want; the angle reads beside it. Drag anywhere on the dial, scroll, or use the arrows (Shift for 1°, else 15° steps, which snap). Double-click returns to data-default. <div class="nk-angle-unit"> <span class="nk-angle" data-value="120" aria-label="Light direction"></span> <output></output> </div>

- classes: `nk-angle`, `nk-angle-cap`, `nk-angle-notch`, `nk-angle-unit`
- modifiers: `is-turning`, `is-zero`

### scale

Scale — the notches under a slider, and around a knob. A slider scale is a row of ticks (data-ticks of them; the ends and the centre longer) with labels spread evenly under it; tied to a slider (data-for) the ticks up to its value light, and a slider whose step matches lands on them. The knob frame puts numbered notches and end labels around a range knob so its travel reads before you touch it. <input class="nk-slider" id="gain" type="range" min="0" max="10" step="1"> (inside a .nk-slider-row it takes the slider's column by itself) <div class="nk-scale" data-for="gain" data-ticks="11" data-labels='["0","5","10"]'></div> <div class="nk-knob-frame" data-ticks="11" data-from="0" data-to="10"><button class="nk-knob" data-min="0" data-max="10" …></button></div>

- classes: `nk-knob-end`, `nk-knob-frame`, `nk-knob-notch`, `nk-scale`, `nk-scale-label`, `nk-scale-tick`, `nk-slider-row`
- modifiers: `is-from`, `is-major`, `is-on`, `is-to`

### dual

Dual pill — two controls that belong together sharing one pill: a main choice and its setting (a material mode and its resolution, a device and its level). A hairline divides them; either half can be a button, a menu trigger or a readout. With one child it is just a pill. From Gouache's viewport toolbar. <div class="nk-dual" role="group" aria-label="Display"> <button class="nk-dual-part">Material</button><button class="nk-dual-part is-value">4K</button> </div>

- classes: `nk-dual`, `nk-dual-part`
- modifiers: `is-value`

### tabs

Tabs — for switching between views of the same thing, with their panels. (The segmented control switches a small mode on hover; tabs are clicked, because a whole view changing under a passing pointer is hostile.) The chosen tab is ink with a short accent bar under it — a lamp, not an underline across the whole row. Arrows move between tabs, Home and End jump to the ends; a tab can carry a count or a lamp. <div class="nk-tabs"> <div class="nk-tabs-list" role="tablist"> <button class="nk-tab" role="tab" aria-selected="true" aria-controls="t1">Overview</button> <button class="nk-tab" role="tab" aria-controls="t2">Logs <span class="nk-tab-count">12</span></button> </div> <div class="nk-tab-panel" role="tabpanel" id="t1">…</div> <div class="nk-tab-panel" role="tabpanel" id="t2" hidden>…</div> </div> Navigation between pages wears the same look but stays links: no tablist, no panels, no arrow keys, and the current page is marked with aria-current (a screen reader then says "current page", not "tab"). <nav class="nk-tabs-list" aria-label="Sections"> <a class="nk-tab" href="overview.html">Overview</a> <a class="nk-tab" href="components.html" aria-current="page">Components</a> </nav>

- classes: `nk-led`, `nk-tab`, `nk-tab-count`, `nk-tab-panel`, `nk-tabs`, `nk-tabs-list`
- modifiers: `is-compact`

### disclosure

Disclosure and accordion — detail that is there when asked for. A native <details class="nk-disclosure">: the summary is a row with a chevron that turns, the body is indented to the summary's text. Several sharing a name="…" make an accordion (the browser keeps one open). A count or a lamp at the end of the summary says what is inside without opening it.

- classes: `nk-disclosure`, `nk-disclosure-body`, `nk-disclosure-meta`

### nav

Breadcrumb and pagination — where you are, and where the rest is. A breadcrumb is for places in an app (sans, chevrons); a file path uses .nk-path (mono). The last crumb is the current page: ink, not a link. Pagination: previous / next shells and the pages between, the current page raised; long runs collapse to an ellipsis.

- classes: `nk-breadcrumb`, `nk-breadcrumb-sep`, `nk-page-btn`, `nk-page-gap`, `nk-pagination`, `nk-pagination-meta`, `nk-path`
- modifiers: `is-step`

### avatar

Avatar — a person or an agent. A machined shell holding a picture or two initials; a square lamp at the corner says whether they are here. Agents (anything that isn't a person) are rounded squares, people are round, so the two never get confused in a chat or a member list. A stack overlaps them, the last one counting the rest.

- classes: `nk-avatar`, `nk-avatars`, `nk-led`
- modifiers: `is-agent`, `is-large`, `is-more`, `is-small`

### combobox

Combobox — type to narrow a long list, or pick from it. An input.nk-input field with a native <datalist> as the source of truth (so forms, and the value, are the browser's own); neuronkit.js shows the matches in the select's menu, the typed part lit in each. Arrows move, Enter picks, Escape closes and keeps what you typed. data-strict refuses a value that isn't in the list. <label class="nk-input nk-combobox"><input list="models" placeholder="Model"></label> <datalist id="models"><option value="qwen3-32b" label="32B · 4-bit">…</datalist>

- classes: `nk-combobox`, `nk-input`, `nk-sel-empty`, `nk-sel-item`
- attributes: `data-state`

### command

Command palette — every action, one keystroke away. A dialog with one large search field; results grouped, each with its icon, a hint and its own shortcut; the highlighted one raised. Opens with Ctrl/⌘+K (or any [data-command="id"] trigger); arrows move, Enter runs, Escape closes. Running an item emits nk:confirm with its data-action. <dialog class="nk-command" id="cmd" data-hotkey="k"> <label class="nk-command-search"><svg…/><input placeholder="Type a command"></label> <div class="nk-command-list"> <div class="nk-command-group">Session</div> <button class="nk-command-item" data-action="new"><svg…/><span>New session</span><kbd class="nk-kbd">N</kbd></button> </div> </dialog>

- classes: `nk-command`, `nk-command-empty`, `nk-command-foot`, `nk-command-group`, `nk-command-item`, `nk-command-list`, `nk-command-search`
- attributes: `data-command`, `data-highlighted`

### toolbar

Toolbar — a row of tools over a canvas or an editor. Groups of icon buttons, segmented modes and dual pills, divided by vertical rules; one Tab stop for the whole bar, arrows move inside it (role="toolbar", kept by neuronkit.js). .is-floating lifts it onto the canvas as a raised face whose corners are concentric with the keys inside it.

- classes: `nk-icon-button`, `nk-rule`, `nk-toolbar`, `nk-toolbar-group`, `nk-toolbar-spacer`
- modifiers: `is-floating`, `is-vertical`

### colour

Colour picker — an instrument, not a gradient box. Hue is a dial: a recessed bezel carrying a ring of square lamps, one per hue, with a machined thumb riding it (a shell carrying a lamp in the pure hue, like the switch). The lamps near the chosen hue light up; the rest stay dim tinted lenses. Saturation and brightness are a recessed window cut into the raised centre cap, with its own machined thumb carrying the chosen colour. Beside the dial, the readings: was / now lenses (press "was" to go back), the hex, HSB | RGB and three scrub fields, each with a track under it showing what that channel does. Drag the ring or the window, scroll the dial, or focus either and use the arrows (Shift for bigger steps). Only the hex leaves the component, as nk:change. <div class="nk-colour" data-value="#e54866"></div> <div class="nk-colour" data-value="#91c9ff" data-was="#79d7b5" data-mode="rgb"></div> <div class="nk-colour is-compact" data-value="#e54866"></div> readings under the dial, for popovers --colour-w is the dial's diameter (232px); in .is-compact, the whole width. The hues and the field's black and white are colour data, the only literal colours here.

- classes: `nk-choice`, `nk-colour`, `nk-colour-area`, `nk-colour-cap`, `nk-colour-dial`, `nk-colour-lamp`, `nk-colour-lens`, `nk-colour-lenses`, `nk-colour-readings`, `nk-colour-ring-thumb`, `nk-colour-row`, `nk-colour-scrubs`, `nk-colour-thumb`, `nk-colour-track`, `nk-input`
- modifiers: `is-compact`, `is-turning`

### drawer

Drawer — a dialog that slides in from an edge: settings, a detail view, a filter panel. Same native <dialog> and behaviours as .nk-dialog (Escape, the backdrop, focus kept inside); data-side picks the edge. On a phone everything becomes a bottom sheet with a grip. <dialog class="nk-drawer" id="d" data-side="right">…</dialog>

- classes: `nk-dialog`, `nk-drawer`, `nk-drawer-head`, `nk-drawer-title`
- modifiers: `is-sheet`
- attributes: `data-side`

### calendar

Calendar and date picker — a month of days on a face. Today carries a lamp under its number; the chosen day is raised and lit in the accent; a range fills the days between. Arrows move by day and week, Page Up/Down by month, Home/End to the week's ends, Enter chooses. The date picker is an input group that opens one in a popover; the value is always ISO (2026-09-27), so it is never ambiguous. <div class="nk-calendar" data-value="2026-09-27"></div> <div class="nk-calendar" data-mode="range" data-from="2026-09-08" data-to="2026-09-15"></div> <label class="nk-input nk-datepicker"><input value="2026-09-27" aria-label="Day"></label>

- classes: `nk-cal-day`, `nk-cal-foot`, `nk-cal-grid`, `nk-cal-head`, `nk-cal-nav`, `nk-cal-title`, `nk-cal-wd`, `nk-calendar`, `nk-datepicker`, `nk-datepicker-btn`, `nk-datepicker-pop`
- modifiers: `is-in`, `is-next`, `is-other`, `is-today`

### range

Range slider — a low and a high on one track: two native range inputs laid on top of each other (so keyboard, forms and screen readers get the real thing), the travel between them lit. neuronkit.js keeps them from crossing and paints the fill. <div class="nk-range" data-unit=" GB"> <input type="range" min="0" max="128" value="16" aria-label="Minimum VRAM"> <input type="range" min="0" max="128" value="96" aria-label="Maximum VRAM"> </div> <output> siblings inside a .nk-slider-row show "16–96 GB".

- classes: `nk-range`, `nk-slider-row`

### otp

One-time code — a row of recessed cells, one character each. Typing moves on, Backspace moves back, pasting fills them all, arrows walk the row. A separator (.nk-otp-sep) splits long codes into readable groups. When the last cell fills, nk:confirm carries the code. <div class="nk-otp" data-length="6" aria-label="Verification code"></div>

- classes: `nk-otp`, `nk-otp-sep`
- modifiers: `has-error`

### taginput

Tag input — values typed into a field become tags inside it. Enter or a comma adds one, Backspace in an empty field takes the last one back, each tag has its own remove. A hidden input (name from data-name) carries the list to a form, comma-separated. <div class="nk-taginput" data-name="labels" data-value='["gpu","render"]'><input placeholder="Add a label"></div>

- classes: `nk-taginput`, `nk-taginput-tag`
- modifiers: `is-armed`

### menubar

Menubar — an application's File · Edit · View. Each item opens a .nk-menu; once one is open, pointing at a neighbour opens that one instead, and Left/Right walk the bar with the menus following. One Tab stop. <nav class="nk-menubar" aria-label="Application"> <button class="nk-menubar-item" data-menu="m-file">File</button> … </nav>

- classes: `nk-menu`, `nk-menubar`, `nk-menubar-item`

### stages

Stages — where a multi-step job is: done, current, still to come. Each stage is a square lamp centred over its name, on one continuous rail. Done stages are lit lamps on a filled rail; the current one is a lit accent ring, and the rail after it fills to --progress (0–1) so the track itself shows how far along the job is (data-progress=".62" on the step: the kit fills the rail and prints the percentage); stages ahead are unlit. A stage that failed carries data-state="crit" and says why in its sub-line. .is-vertical stacks them, left-aligned, for a sidebar or a long job. <ol class="nk-stages"> <li data-state="done"><b>Download</b><span>19 GB</span></li> <li aria-current="step" style="--progress:.62"><b>Quantise</b><span>4-bit · 62%</span></li> <li><b>Load</b></li> </ol>

- classes: `nk-stages`, `nk-stages-pct`
- modifiers: `is-vertical`
- attributes: `data-sep`, `data-state`

### timeline

Timeline — what happened, newest first: the time in mono, a lamp on a rail (toned when the event matters), a title and an optional line of detail. Quiet events stay unlit, so the ones that went wrong stand out. <ol class="nk-timeline"> <li data-tone="crit"><time>12:41</time><b>ledger-api unhealthy</b><p>GET /healthz 503</p></li> <li><time>12:02</time><b>Deployed v2.4.1</b></li> </ol>

- classes: `nk-timeline`
- attributes: `data-tone`

### spark

Sparkline — a trend in the space of a word, for a row, a stat or a table cell. One grey line over a faint area, its last point a dot; toned only when the trend itself is the problem. Drawn by neuronkit.js from data-values (null = a gap), redrawn when they change. In a row, an empty .nk-row-value prints the last reading (with data-unit), "—" when it is a gap. <span class="nk-spark" data-values="[3,4,4,6,5,8,7,9]"></span> <span class="nk-spark" data-tone="warn" data-values="[…]" style="--spark-w:120px"></span>

- classes: `nk-row-value`, `nk-spark`, `nk-spark-area`, `nk-spark-end`, `nk-spark-line`
- attributes: `data-tone`

### banner

Banner — one message for the whole page, above everything: a maintenance window, a licence about to lapse, an update ready. A lamp says how much it matters, one action at most, and it can be dismissed unless it can't be ignored. Never more than one at a time. <div class="nk-banner" data-tone="warn" role="status"> <span class="nk-led" data-tone="warn"></span><p>Maintenance tonight 22:00–23:00 UTC.</p> <a href="#">Details</a><button class="nk-banner-close" aria-label="Dismiss"></button> </div>

- classes: `nk-banner`, `nk-banner-close`
- modifiers: `is-floating`

### sortable

Sortable list — rows you put in order by their grip: drag it, or focus it, press Space to lift the row, arrows to move it, Space to set it down (Escape puts it back). The lifted row is a raised shell; the others make room as it passes. nk:change carries the new order (each row's data-value). Layers, playlists, priorities. <ul class="nk-sortable" aria-label="Layers"> <li class="nk-sortable-item" data-value="base"><button class="nk-sortable-grip" aria-label="Move Base"></button>Base colour</li> </ul>

- classes: `nk-sortable`, `nk-sortable-grip`, `nk-sortable-item`, `nk-sorting`
- modifiers: `is-lifted`

### chart

Chart — a time series with axes, for monitoring: the reading over the last hour, against its limit. Lines are the ink ladder (the first series in ink, the next ones quieter); the stretch of a line past its limit turns --err, because that stretch is the problem. The limit is a dashed hairline with its value printed on it. Hover, or focus and use the arrows, to read any point in a floating readout; null is a gap, never a zero. Drawn by neuronkit.js at the chart's real size, redrawn when it resizes or its data changes. <figure class="nk-chart" data-series='[{"name":"GPU0 junction","values":[71,72,74]}]' data-start="2026-09-28T13:00:00Z" data-step="60" data-unit="°C" data-limit="95"></figure> data-min / data-max fix the scale (0–100 for percentages); --chart-h sets the plot height (default 180px). A series with "tone" takes that state colour instead of ink. el.nkPush(v, …) adds one reading per series.

- classes: `nk-chart`, `nk-chart-area`, `nk-chart-cursor`, `nk-chart-dot`, `nk-chart-empty`, `nk-chart-end`, `nk-chart-grid`, `nk-chart-legend`, `nk-chart-limit`, `nk-chart-line`, `nk-chart-readout`, `nk-chart-tick`
- modifiers: `is-base`, `is-over`
- attributes: `data-tone`

### log

Log view — a service's output, live. A filter field, a level bank (all · warnings · errors, with the error count on it) and a line count over the lines themselves: mono, one per row, time dimmed, message in muted ink. Only errors and warnings carry a lamp and a faint tone wash, so a healthy log reads as quiet grey and a bad line stands out. ANSI colours map onto the state colours. It follows the newest line until you scroll up; then a pill counts what arrived and takes you back. Only the rows on screen exist (neuronkit.js virtualises), so thousands of lines stay light. <div class="nk-log" aria-label="ledger-api"><pre> 2026-09-28T13:02:09Z INFO listening on :8080 2026-09-28T13:04:41Z ERROR GET /healthz 503</pre></div> log(el, lines) appends; el.nkSet(lines) replaces. --log-h sets the height (default 320px), data-max the lines kept (default 5000).

- classes: `nk-ansi-blue`, `nk-ansi-bold`, `nk-ansi-dim`, `nk-ansi-green`, `nk-ansi-magenta`, `nk-ansi-red`, `nk-ansi-yellow`, `nk-led`, `nk-log`, `nk-log-bar`, `nk-log-body`, `nk-log-count`, `nk-log-empty`, `nk-log-filter`, `nk-log-jump`, `nk-log-lamp`, `nk-log-line`, `nk-log-rows`, `nk-log-spacer`, `nk-log-text`
- attributes: `data-level`

## css/flow.css (opt-in)

NeuronKit theme for SvelteFlow (@xyflow/svelte). Load after the library's own stylesheet and neuronkit.css. Maps nodes, handles, edges, controls and the minimap onto the kit's faces and ink — no new colours.

- classes: `nk-flow`, `nk-node`, `nk-node-branch`, `nk-node-head`, `nk-node-meta`, `nk-node-title`

## css/social.css (opt-in)

NeuronKit — social posts. Opt-in (load after neuronkit.css): the kit's identity at poster scale, for carousels, stories and avatars. A post is a fixed canvas (.nk-post, 1080 × 1350 by default); everything inside is in poster pixels, so a template renders the same in a browser, a headless export or a design review. The accent is the page's (data-accent), so one template gives a Cherry, Mint or Lapis series. <section class="nk-post"> 4:5 carousel slide <header class="nk-post-top"><span class="nk-post-brand"><img src="logo.svg" alt="">BRAND <b>·</b> LAB</span> <span class="nk-post-step"><i class="nk-post-lamp"></i>1 / 3</span></header> <h1 class="nk-post-title">Memes hide in the <em>transcript</em>.</h1> <p class="nk-post-lede">…</p> <div class="nk-post-card"><span class="nk-post-label"><i class="nk-post-lamp"></i>Prompt</span><p>…</p></div> <p class="nk-post-tip"><i class="nk-post-lamp"></i>…</p> <footer class="nk-post-foot"><span>…</span><b>Swipe →</b></footer> </section> .is-story (1080 × 1920) · .is-square (1080 × 1080) · .nk-post-avatar for a profile picture.

- classes: `nk-post`, `nk-post-avatar`, `nk-post-brand`, `nk-post-card`, `nk-post-chips`, `nk-post-cta`, `nk-post-foot`, `nk-post-instrument`, `nk-post-key`, `nk-post-keys`, `nk-post-label`, `nk-post-lamp`, `nk-post-lede`, `nk-post-phone`, `nk-post-safe`, `nk-post-step`, `nk-post-tip`, `nk-post-title`, `nk-post-top`, `nk-post-vignette`

## Svelte 5 wrappers (svelte/, `import { … } from "neuronkit/svelte"`)

- **Button** — <Button variant="primary" onclick={…}>Save</Button> · href makes it a link. tone="ok" and icon="check" make it a dynamic button (tint + icon on hover).   
  props: `variant = "", href, type = "button", tone, icon, motion, children, ...rest`
- **IconButton** — <IconButton label="Settings" icon="settings" /> — or pass your own svg as children. pressed makes it a toggle (aria-pressed). The label is the tooltip too.   
  props: `label, icon, pressed, tooltip = true, children, ...rest`
- **Switch** — <Switch bind:checked label="Autostart" />   
  props: `checked = $bindable(false), label, disabled = false, onchange, ...rest`
- **Checkbox** — <Checkbox bind:checked>Watch this peer</Checkbox>   
  props: `checked = $bindable(false), disabled = false, children, ...rest`
- **Select** — <Select bind:value options={[{ value, label, desc?, disabled? }]} label="Edge" /> A native <select> stays the source of truth; neuronkit.js draws the menu. An option with desc gets a second line.   
  props: `value = $bindable(), options = [], label, hint, placeholder, disabled = false, id = nkId("select"), onchange`
- **Combobox** — <Combobox bind:value options={[{ value, label? }]} label="Model" strict />   
  props: `value = $bindable(""), options = [], label, hint, placeholder, strict = false, id = nkId("combo"), onchange`
- **Slider** — <Slider bind:value min={0} max={10} step={1} label="Steps" ticks={11} labels={["0","5","10"]} />   
  props: `value = $bindable(0), min = 0, max = 100, step = 1, unit, label, ticks, labels, disabled = false, id = nkId("slider"), onchange`
- **Knob** — <Knob bind:value min={0} max={100} unit="%" label="Volume" icon="speaker" /> A continuous knob: drag, scroll or arrows (Shift fine), double-click resets. ticks={11} adds the notched frame with from/to labels at its ends.   
  props: `value = $bindable(0), min = 0, max = 100, step = 1, default: def, unit = "", bipolar = false, icon, color, label, showValue = false, size, ticks, from, to, onchange`
- **Wheel** — <Wheel bind:value min={0} max={359} unit="°" wrap label="Light rotation" /> A thumbwheel: drag along it (Shift fine), scroll, arrows; double-click resets.   
  props: `value = $bindable(0), min = 0, max = 1, step, default: def, unit = "", wrap = false, vertical = false, label, disabled = false, readout = true, onchange`
- **Angle** — <Angle bind:value label="Light direction" /> — 0° up, clockwise.   
  props: `value = $bindable(0), default: def = 0, label = "Angle", size, disabled = false, readout = true, onchange`
- **Scrub** — <Scrub bind:value label="Roughness" min={0} max={1} step={0.01} /> Drag the label sideways (Shift ×0.1, Ctrl ×10) or type the number.   
  props: `value = $bindable(0), label, min, max, step = 0.01, disabled = false, onchange`
- **Colour** — <Colour bind:value /> — a hex string. A hue dial of lamps with a saturation / brightness window in its cap, and the readings (was / now, hex, HSB | RGB). width = the dial's diameter (or the whole width when compact); was = the "was" lens (defaults to the first value); compact stacks the readings under the dial, for popovers; mode = "hsb" | "rgb".   
  props: `value = $bindable("#e54866"), width, was, compact = false, mode, onchange`
- **Tabs** — <Tabs bind:value tabs={[{ id, label, count?, tone?, disabled? }]}>{#snippet panel(tab)}…{/snippet}</Tabs> Clicked, not hovered; arrows, Home and End move — neuronkit.js does it, the same code as a plain page.   
  props: `tabs = [], value = $bindable(tabs[0]?.id), compact = false, panel, onchange`
- **Dialog** — <Dialog bind:open title="Restart ledger-api?" description="…">body{#snippet actions()}…{/snippet}</Dialog> side="right" | "left" | "bottom" makes it a drawer. A button with data-dialog-close closes it (its value becomes the return value).   
  props: `open = $bindable(false), title, description, side, tone, children, actions, onclose`
- **Menu** — <Menu label="Session actions" items={[{ label, action, desc?, kbd?, danger?, disabled?, separator? }]} onselect={(action) => …}> {#snippet trigger()}⋯{/snippet} </Menu> context makes it a right-click menu on the children instead of a button.   
  props: `items = [], label = "Menu", heading, context = false, trigger, children, onselect`
- **CommandPalette** — <CommandPalette groups={[{ label, items: [{ label, action, hint?, kbd?, keywords? }] }]} onrun={(action) => …} /> Ctrl/⌘ + hotkey opens it (default K); bind:open to open it from code.   
  props: `groups = [], hotkey = "k", placeholder = "Type a command or search", open = $bindable(false), onrun`
- **Meter** — <Meter label="Memory" frac={0.41} value="41%" tone="warn" /> — the segmented meter.   
  props: `label, frac = 0, value, tone`
- **Led** — <Led tone="ok" /> — ok · warn · crit · busy · info · idle. Say the state in words beside it too.   
  props: `tone = "idle", label`
- **Calendar** — <Calendar bind:value /> — ISO date. range: <Calendar range bind:from bind:to />   
  props: `value = $bindable(""), from = $bindable(""), to = $bindable(""), range = false, min, max, weekStart, onchange`
- **DatePicker** — <DatePicker bind:value label="Render on" /> — ISO, typeable, with a calendar.   
  props: `value = $bindable(""), label, min, max, id = nkId("date"), onchange`
- **RangeSlider** — <RangeSlider bind:low bind:high min={0} max={128} step={4} unit=" GB" label="VRAM" />   
  props: `low = $bindable(0), high = $bindable(100), min = 0, max = 100, step = 1, unit = "", label, onchange`
- **CodeInput** — <CodeInput bind:value length={6} oncomplete={(code) => …} /> — a one-time code.   
  props: `value = $bindable(""), length = 6, label = "Verification code", alpha = false, oncomplete`
- **TagInput** — <TagInput bind:value placeholder="Add a label" name="labels" /> — value is an array of strings.   
  props: `value = $bindable([]), placeholder, name, label = "Tags", onchange`
- **Sortable** — <Sortable bind:items label="Layers">{#snippet row(item)}{item.name}{/snippet}</Sortable> items: [{ id, … }]. neuronkit.js moves the rows; the new order comes back as items.   
  props: `items = $bindable([]), label, row, onchange`
- **Spark** — <Spark values={[3,4,6,5,8]} tone="warn" width={96} /> — null is a gap.   
  props: `values = [], tone, width, height, label`
- **Chart** — <Chart series={[{ name: "GPU0 junction", values: [71, 72, null, 74] }]} start={t0} step={60} unit="°C" limit={95} /> A time series with axes; the stretch past the limit turns red. null is a gap. Hover or arrow keys read a point. Change series (or push into it) and it redraws.   
  props: `series = [], start, step = 60, unit = "", limit, min, max, height, label`
- **LogView** — <LogView lines={lines} label="ledger-api" /> — lines are strings ("2026-09-28T12:38:12Z ERROR …") or { t, level, text }. Push onto the array and only the new lines are added; replace it with a shorter one and the view starts over. Filter, levels and follow-the-tail come from neuronkit.js, the same as on a plain page.   
  props: `lines = [], label = "Log", height, max`

Helpers: `nk` (use:nk action, forwards nk:change / nk:confirm), `nkId`, `enhance`, `toast`, `icon`.
